drills.title: The late fee
drills.prompt: Arrange the lines into the library's late-fee calculation: a book borrowed on 1 Nov and returned on 20 Nov, a 14-day loan period and Rs. 5 per late day. Two lines do not belong.
drills.explain: ChronoUnit.DAYS.between returns a long, so it cannot be stored in an int without a cast (the compiler reports a lossy conversion). Math.max(0, days - 14) keeps the late days from going negative for an early return, and the (int) cast turns the long into the int fee. LocalDate has no public constructor: use parse or of.

drills.title: Check the rules before changing anything
drills.prompt: Fill the blanks so checkout rejects an unknown or sold-out book with a LibraryError and only changes the stock when every rule has passed.
code: private final Map<String, Integer> copies = new TreeMap<>();
drills.explain: Map has containsKey (not contains or hasKey) and put, which also replaces an existing value. Both checks come before put, so a failed checkout leaves the stock exactly as it was: the output still shows B1=0 from the first, successful call. LibraryError extends RuntimeException, so callers are not forced to catch it; extending Exception would make every checkout declare throws.

drills.title: Records never change
drills.prompt: Read the code and type exactly what it prints, one line per line of output.
code: record Book(String isbn, String title, int copies) {
Book withMoreCopies(int extra) { return new Book(isbn, title, copies + extra); }
drills.explain: A record cannot change, so withMoreCopies builds a new Book with 5 copies and put stores it under the same key. The original dune object still has 2 copies. equals on records compares all the components (so the second Book("B1", "Dune", 2) is equal), and toString prints the type with name=value pairs.

drills.title: The line that split into letters
drills.prompt: load reads one saved line, BOOK|B1|Dune|3, but the program crashes. Click the faulty line, then choose the fix.
drills.explain: split takes a regular expression, and | means "or" in a regex, so split("|") cuts the line after every character. part[3] is then the letter K, and parseInt fails. To match a real bar, escape it for the regex (\|) and escape the backslash for Java (\\|). A single \| is not a legal Java string escape, and split('|') passes a char instead of a String.

drills.title: Review the AI's Library class
drills.prompt: An AI assistant wrote this part of the library system. It compiles and runs, but tick the real problems (there are three).
code: private final List<Loan> loans = new ArrayList<>();

issues.text: checkout adds the loan first and checks the limit afterwards
issues.why: When the rule fails, the exception is thrown but the extra loan is already in the list, so the failed checkout changed the library. Check loansOf(member) >= MAX_LOANS first and add the loan last.

== asks whether both variables are the same object, not whether the names match. It happens to work with two literals in main, but a name read from a file or typed by a user is a different object and is never counted. Use loan.member().equals(member).

issues.text: lateFee goes negative for a book returned on time
issues.why: Returned after 9 days, days - LOAN_DAYS is -5 and the fee is -25, as if the library paid the member. Use Math.max(0, days - LOAN_DAYS) so only late days are charged.

non_issues.text: Loan should be a normal class with setters, so loans can be edited
non_issues.why: A record is the right tool for plain data that should not change after creation. To change a loan you build a new one.

non_issues.text: lateFee returns a long, so it must be cast to int
non_issues.why: Nothing requires an int here. The long that comes from ChronoUnit is returned as it is and prints normally.

non_issues.text: The three constants should be instance fields
non_issues.why: Fixed rules that are the same for every library belong in private static final constants, and the names tell the reader what 14, 5 and 2 mean.

non_issues.text: loansOf loops over the list instead of using a Map
non_issues.why: For a few loans a simple loop is clear and correct. A Map could be added later if the numbers grow.

drills.explain: In rule-heavy classes check the order inside each method (rules first, changes last), the way text values are compared (equals, not ==) and the edge cases of every formula (what happens at zero or below zero?).
